interventions.speaker: CHAIR
interventions.who: the senior urologist who signs the decision
interventions.body: The prognosis is influenced by several factors, including the positive surgical margins and the presence of lymph node metastasis documented in the pathology report. The preoperative PSA was 4.1 ng/mL, which contributes to the risk assessment. A countervailing finding is that seminal vesicle invasion was absent, and lymphovascular invasion was also negative. Biopsy findings (Gleason 3+4) align with the prostatectomy specimen grade (ISUP group 2). The nodal status was documented as positive for metastasis. Missing postoperative PSA data prevents a more refined assessment of current disease burden. Future prognosis would be significantly revised by obtaining serial postoperative PSA measurements and tracking their trajectory over time. The fixed estimated horizon is 62.79 months. This represents expected follow-up without an event, not a known recurrence date. The sensitivity range is 50.23–75.35 months; its coverage has not been validated.
